threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: C++ lets a program take addresses, hold references and call an allocator, so this class is applicable. The gates take and return int by value (code/packages/cpp/logic-gates/include/logic_gates/logic_gates.hpp:96-177) and keep no object alive past a call. The only object with a lifetime is on the rejection path: a std::string temporary and the exception object, both owned by RAII (std::string destructor; the runtime frees the exception object after the catch). A use after free needs a free the package never calls itself, but the reject path does allocate and free, so "no allocation" cannot be asserted.

threats.name: Out-of-bounds Write
threats.rationale: Out-of-bounds write needs an index, a pointer offset or a copy into a buffer. The library has none: no array, no index, no pointer arithmetic, no memcpy. The one buffer is the std::string built on the rejection path, which the standard library bounds-manages. Children 121, 122 and 124 are covered by this row.

threats.name: Out-of-bounds Read
threats.rationale: Out-of-bounds read needs an index or a pointer that can run past an object. The only pointers are const char* parameters bound to the string literals "a" and "b" (code/packages/cpp/logic-gates/include/logic_gates/logic_gates.hpp:97, :103-104) that std::string reads up to the terminating NUL, and the literal is never indexed or offset by the library. Children 126 and 127 are covered by this row. Today detail::reject is public (logic_gates::detail::reject) and takes a const char* that a caller can point at any memory, after which std::string reads up to a NUL: an out-of-bounds read reachable through the shipped header until the int-only helper change.

No gate is declared [[nodiscard]] (code/packages/cpp/logic-gates/include/logic_gates/logic_gates.hpp:96-177). closed_by.detail: Every public function is declared [[nodiscard]] (C++17), so a discarded result is a diagnostic under -Werror in the consumer. The cpp analyzer is not built; its grammar front end is LGE-A2.

threats.name: Braced-init-list arguments bypass the deleted overloads
threats.rationale: Braced-init-list arguments skip the deleted templates: a template parameter cannot be deduced from {true}, so only the non-template int overload is viable and the list-initialisation of the int parameter from {true}, {b} (a bool variable) or {'a'} (a char) succeeds. Reproduced with the local clang++: and_gate({true}, 1) returns 1, not_gate({true}) returns 0, and_gate({b}, 1) returns 1, and and_gate({'a'}, 1) compiles and throws "got 97" at run time. clang++ warns (-Wbraced-scalar-init); g++ and MSVC are silent as far as the review found. The header presents the deleted overloads as the CWE-843 and CWE-704 defence (code/packages/cpp/logic-gates/include/logic_gates/logic_gates.hpp:45-57) and the tests probe plain-expression calls only (code/packages/cpp/logic-gates/tests/logic_gates_test.cpp:34-55), so the hole is unrecorded in the package. The values that get through are valid-looking bits (a bool) or are rejected at run time (a char), so this is a type-confusion hole, not a memory error.

closed_by.detail: Each gate has a deleted catch-all function template (code/packages/cpp/logic-gates/include/logic_gates/logic_gates.hpp:185-196); an exact int call prefers the non-template, every other argument type deduces exactly and selects the deleted template, so the call does not compile. Holds for calls with plain-expression arguments only (see cpp.braced-init-list-bypass and cpp.deleted-overload-bypass-via-indirection).

LG02 section 9 for a statically typed lane: void_t traits prove a direct call with bool, char, signed char, unsigned char, short, unsigned, long, unsigned long, long long, float or double is ill-formed, in each argument position of all eleven gates (code/packages/cpp/logic-gates/tests/logic_gates_test.cpp:28-103), and that int is accepted so the traits are not vacuous (code/packages/cpp/logic-gates/tests/logic_gates_test.cpp:57-63). Plain-expression direct calls only: no braced-init-list row ({true}, {b}, {'a'}), no indirect call (function pointer, std::function, std::invoke), no string-literal, enum, wchar_t, char16_t, char32_t, nullptr_t, unsigned short, unsigned long long, long double, class-with-conversion-operator row.

Deleted std::initializer_list<T> overloads (or a deleted catch-all that also matches a braced-init-list) for every gate, so and_gate({true}, 1) does not compile. Planned in LGE-CPP-HARDEN (local, in progress).

Negative-compile tests: every deleted-overload row, the braced-init-list rows and the invalid-constant-expression row must fail to compile (a test that compiles is a failure). Planned in LGE-CPP-HARDEN.

Every public function has a deleted catch-all function template and a deleted std::initializer_list overload of the same name, so no future gate can be added without the type-confusion guards (logic_gates.hpp:185-196 lists eleven templates; the rule checks the list against the defined functions). The cpp analyzer is not built; its grammar front end is LGE-A2.
